text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The Vietnamese government is planning to provide jobs for nearly 1.5 million people next year and for 6.5 million by 2000. Among the jobs targeted for 1997 are 20,000 in South Korea, Taiwan, Iraq and Kuwait.
-- Many National Assembly delegates want those responsible for allowing the import of luxury goods and obsolete equipment to explain themselves.

-- Sedona Hotels International, a Singapore-based hotel management and development company, is planning to launch serviced apartments in Vietnam as early as next month. Apartments in Hanoi are set to follow in the first quarter of next year.

-- A $68 million joint venture project between Malaysia's Go Hoch Guan Group and the Vietnam Import-Export Company to build a hotel and entertainment complex near the northern resort area of Halong Bay has been granted a license.
-- National Assembly delegates have called for wage reforms and raised concern over inefficient efforts to combat corruption.
-- Authorities in Hanoi have launched a campaign to counter drug abuse in schools and colleges.
-- Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi has told teachers and scientists that the party and government was concerned about corruption and moral degeneration.
-- Water levels in the Mekong Delta have continued a slight fall. But, with the biggest tide of the year due next week, flooding will become more serious in lower stretches of the river.
